did.abstract: Volume, in multiple hands, of seven booklets primarily on such topics as law, Parliament, government, and public finances. Parliamentary items include speeches by Thomas Wentworth, earl of Strafford, and Francis Seymour, Baron Trowbridge, complaining about forced loans, billeting of soldiers, and other grievances; a copy of the Spanish ambassador's complaints against George Villiers, Duke of Buckingham, as well as his own excuses for the conduct of the Spanish during marriage negotiations between Charles I and the Infanta Maria; a Parliamentary grievance against Buckingham; and journal notes for the House of Lords in 1621.

did.unittitle: "A Briefe Collection of all generall Penall Statutes now in force..."

descriptivenote.p: "A Briefe Collection of all generall Penall Statutes now in force..."

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p:
32 p.
Autograph MS.
The statutes are arranged under
general hearings, with a brief
explanation accompanying. Signature
of John Browne appears on first page.
f.I.

did.unittitle: CHARLES I, KING OF GREAT BRITAIN, 1600-1649
[Speech delivered at the opening of Parliament, 1627/8 Mar 17]

descriptivenote.p: [Speech delivered at the opening of Parliament, 1627/8 Mar 17]

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p:
2 p.
Contemporary MS copy.
Requests supply for defense of realm
and expresses willingness to forget
distractions of the last Parliament.
Rushworth, v.i, p.476-477.
f.IIa

descriptivenote.p: [Speech in Parliament, 1627/8 March 22]

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p:
1 p.
Contemporary MS copy.
Demands redress of grievances before
supply granted; grievances include
forced loan, billeting of soldiers,
imprisonment of gentlemen, etc.
Rushworth, i, p.499-500.
f.IIb

descriptivenote.p: [Speech in Parliament, 1627/8 March 22]

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p:
1 p.
Contemporary MS copy.
Speaks against forced loans and other
grievances.
Rushworth, vii, 500-501.
f.IIc.

descriptivenote.p: [Propositions sent to the House of Commons by the King concerning supply, 1628 Mar 26]

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p:
1 p.
Contemporary MS copy.
Rushworth, i, 513.
f.IId.

descriptivenote.p: [Speech in Parliament, 1628/9 Jan 26]

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p:
4 p.
Contemporary MS copy.

religion, especially Arminianism.
Rushworth, i, 645-646.
f.IIe.

did.unittitle: GREAT BRITAIN. PARLIAMENT, 1626. HOUSE OF COMMONS.

descriptivenote.p: [Declaration to the Lords, 1626 Mar 8 or 9]

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p:
1 p.
Contemporary MS copy.

descriptivenote.p: [Speech in Parliament, 1628 June 3]

14 p.

did.unittitle: GREAT BRITAIN. PARLIAMENT, 1628. HOUSE OF COMMONS.

scopecontent.p:
17 p.
Contemporary MS copy.

scopecontent.p:
4 p.
Contemporary MS copy.
Complaints of the duke's all-

Rushworth, i, 145.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p:
Contemporary MS. Memorandum of

descriptivenote.p: [Questions of the King on points of constitutional law and replies of the judges, c.1628]

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p:
8 p.
Contemporary MS copy in the hand of
John Browne. Includes the three
questions on habeas corpus put to the

April 1629. Also an opinion of
scutage.
f.IIIf.
